status_summary: The coordination half has been resolved by a court rather than by legislation or an FEC rule. On 2026-06-30 the Supreme Court held in NRSC v. FEC (No. 24-621), 6 to 3, that FECA's limits on party coordinated expenditures violate the First Amendment and that Colorado Republican II no longer stands; the government agreed with the challengers that the limits were unconstitutional. The contribution-limit half has not moved: the FEC's 2026 inflation notice (published 2026-03-03) indexes the coordinated expenditure limits and the lobbyist bundling threshold under existing law, and no statute raising contribution limits or indexing other reporting thresholds was found. The opinion treats base contribution limits as valid anti-circumvention tools and leaves them in place; commentary after the ruling says other limits could face later challenges.

timeline.event: FEC publishes its annual price index notice setting 2026 coordinated party expenditure limits and the lobbyist bundling threshold under existing statutory indexing; a footnote says the Supreme Court is considering the limits' constitutionality in NRSC v. FEC.

Supreme Court decides NRSC v. FEC: Justice Kavanaugh writes for six justices (Roberts, Thomas, Alito, Gorsuch, Barrett joining) that the party coordinated expenditure limits violate the First Amendment and that Colorado Republican II is overruled; Justice Kagan dissents with Justices Sotomayor and Jackson. The Court notes the government agreed with the challengers.
